description:
<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="drift-coherence-review" -->

**Drift & Coherence Review (run 4, trend vs the 2026-11-05 run 3 edition)** is the trend-aware periodical (`drift-coherence` in `lib/periodicals.js`, series anchor LIN-369). It looks for code that is locally right while the system as a whole drifts apart. **This task is the review itself.** You write the report, mint the highest-severity follow-ups, get an adversarial second-read, merge the report PR, and then conclude this task. Assume a cold hand-off: all you have is this description plus access to the repos and Linear.

**Operator note.** This run is also read as a **top-down, independent reading for the Survey research** (`docs/plans/survey/notes-2026-11-05.md`, `docs/plans/survey/log.md` and `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`). That is context for what the readings are used for, not extra scope: **do not edit that branch, and do not shape findings to fit it.** Measure the window from the previous edition in this series to main HEAD, and **say plainly whether the window's changes left their areas better or worse.** Form that verdict from the code before you read the place ledger's own balance column; then, if a finding bears on a ledger row, cross-link it in one line and say whether you agree. A disagreement with the ledger is a valid, useful result.

**Repos in remit:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour, primary), `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` (SD), and the runner kit inside Harbour (`lib/runner-kit/`, `docs/runner-prompt.md`). The cross-repo contract between them (runner contract table, halt, markers, the parked-wait text, consumer heartbeat, the model/effort/harness vocabulary, and the per-request usage records) is a seam no sibling review owns, so it belongs to this review.

**The shape of this window.** It is almost entirely Survey-driven work: tickets filed as "tidy first" (before a feature) and "tidy after" (consolidating the edges a feature's blind reads named), plus a large test-infrastructure consolidation (the shared fake DOM). Many commit titles claim "one X" consolidations. **Verify each claim against the code; a title is not evidence.** SD has no commits in the window. A report that is mostly "unchanged / held" for the carried ledger plus a close read of what moved is the expected shape. Do not widen the window, invent make-work, re-flag the 11-05 ledger as new, or pad the report to match the previous edition's length. Say plainly how big the window was and what that did to the confidence of each "unchanged".

---

## What to do

* **Audit the scope before executing.** Treat the scope above as a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for what is *in-remit but unlisted* and fold it in. Candidates to check: the test tree as a home for repeated decisions now that it has its own census-guarded convention (the census tool's scope pattern excludes `tests/`; decide whether a test-side reading belongs in this edition and say why); the Survey stage templates as a new consumer of the preamble, dispatch-entrance and action-kind decisions; `scripts/delivery-paths.mjs` / `scripts/delivery-composition.mjs` against the stage-route table; `public/llms.txt` and `lib/proxy-instructions.js` edits against the preamble's ladder (two texts telling an agent the same thing); `experiments/place-change/place-change.mjs` (a new instrument on main: is it a second census that restates `scripts/code-shape/`?). Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**: the wider scope changes *what you examine*, not *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome), and the follow-up bound below stays as it is.
* **Read prior runs first. This review is trend-aware.** Read the 11-05 report in full (Headline, Method, Findings, Cross-repo contract verdicts, Sibling hand-offs, Classes and bounds, Follow-ups, For John, Ticket trend, Adversarial second-read, the census tables and the Compact trend ledger), then `drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04-run2.md` as background. Frame every finding as a delta against 11-05: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved, never a point-in-time snapshot.
* **Run the review.** This review works at the cross-cutting altitude (locally right, globally drifting), distinct from the per-module Code Quality Review; do not re-flag what it owns. Use the repo's own conventions as the reference, introducing no new tooling. Assess: *duplication* (a decision re-implemented where one shared implementation is canonical; coincidental similarity is fine); *convention fragmentation* (competing patterns where one is canonical; flag the outliers); *dependency direction* (imports against the repo's own layering, for example a core module reaching into a route); and the *cross-repo contract* (Harbour ↔ SD ↔ runner kit). Name the concrete cost a change would hit, not a style preference; no cosmetic churn. Do not find repeated decisions by eye: run the committed census tool (above) at HEAD and at the commit the previous report measured, with one area guide for both runs; record the full commits. Give every `mustRule` group one ruling in a compact table: real (the one place the decision should live and why, or both claimants and your pick), borderline or noise, with a one-line reason; a ruling is your finding, not a question to anyone. List the table groups in one compact table, no ruling. Prose and follow-up tasks only for real groups and for changes since the previous edition. The finding-classes above are **examples, not a limit. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.**
* **Answer the operator's question directly.** Add a short **"Better or worse, by area"** section near the top: for each area the window's production commits touched (at least: stage templates and preamble; the cost read; Go / Home / task-page state; the client test tree), one line with a verdict (better / neutral / worse / mixed) and the evidence (copies added or removed, census groups moved, new homeless files, lines net). Then a one-line overall verdict for the window. Form it from the code; compare it to the Survey place ledger afterwards and record agreement or disagreement per ticket, without editing the branch.
* **Write an uncapped, trend-framed report.** The deliverable is a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found; finding nothing, one thing or several are all valid; do not pad, cap or invent make-work, and a clean result is a genuine outcome. Ground each finding against the source at HEAD, not prior prose. Close the report with the compact trend ledger: every row of the 11-05 ledger under its stable name, with its severity and its delta against 11-05, plus any new rows.
* **Mint a bounded set of follow-up tasks: highest-severity only.** Create at most the top \~3 by severity in Linear (fewer is fine; zero is valid when nothing rises to that bar). Each is well-scoped: a title, and a description that carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. A fix idea is allowed but goes under an "Unvalidated idea" heading, so later stages treat it as a hypothesis. Leave each in its default state (earlier editions parented follow-ups under LIN-3449 with kind:follow-up; follow that if a ticket is minted). **Before minting, search for an existing ticket already naming the same finding** (11-05's "Considered and not minted" table and its search phrases are the model); if one exists, note it in the report instead of minting a duplicate. Record EVERY finding in the report, including the ones not promoted. Err toward under-creating: the Backlog holds the unmoved Drift-family tickets 11-05 lists (`coherence-loop-stalled`), so check which have moved and weigh whether a new ticket will be worked before minting it, and say why.
* **Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude. This is a required, structural step, not advice.** After the report and any follow-up tasks are written, and before the Done transition, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent carrying no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this same session re-reading its own report "from a cold stance") **is not accepted**; state which of Tier 1 or Tier 2 you used. Then post **one** comment on this task holding, together in a single body: `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`; `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict); and `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`. The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. **AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation**, never a reason to leave this task open.
* **Merge your own report PR.** This task owns it. Once its required CI checks (`ci-success`) are green, merge it before the Done transition. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, required checks still red) may this task conclude with the PR open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment. An open report PR is not a normal terminal state.
* **Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task, with a link to the merged report (a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, which the report gate needs) and the one-line better/worse verdict. Then move this task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely; the follow-up tasks carry the actionable work forward.
* **Stay review-only.** Producing the report changes no code, config, guide or secrets in either repo, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence. Do not edit the Survey branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's own deliverable.

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The asker wants to know, **by area, whether the Survey tidy-first/tidy-after window left LinearViewer better or worse**, and whether the 11-05 drift ledger still holds. Done, to them, is:

1. `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-05-run4.md` + `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-05-drift-run4/` merged to main via a docs-only PR (`ci-success` green). If the build runs on a later date, use that date's plain names when free; never overwrite an earlier edition.
2. The report has a "Better or worse, by area" section near the top (stage templates and preamble; cost read; Go/Home/task page; client test tree; one overall line), formed from code *before* the Survey place ledger is read, then compared to it per ticket.
3. All 130 rows of the 11-05 ledger carried under their stable names with a delta each; new rows added; every finding framed new/unchanged/improved/worsened/resolved.
4. At most \~3 follow-ups minted (this plan expects 1), none duplicating an existing ticket.
5. One comment on LIN-4299 with a GitHub blob/commit/PR URL **and** the three second-read fields in one body (`lib/periodical-report-gate.js`), then Done.

The ticket has not drifted from its purpose. Two of its guesses are wrong and the report should say so rather than build on them: `scripts/delivery-paths.mjs` is a shared-helper extraction (`isTest`/`isDoc`), not a stage-route table; `experiments/place-change/place-change.mjs` wraps `seams.mjs` and restates only the guide's area-match rule (borderline/noise, unowned per Stability F10).

### Shape of the work and why (decisions, not code)

This is a review, so the "change" is a docs-only report. The decisions that are expensive to redo once the report exists:

* **Measure mechanically, then read.** The instrument runs first and decides what is "unchanged"; prose is written after. Reason: a title is not evidence ("one X" commit titles), and 11-05's own lesson (row 77) is that census "gone" overstates resolution.
* **One guide, both ends.** Use `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` (sha256 `e3194f52…`, 0-line diff across the window) for both census runs, same `--include '^(server\.js$|(lib|routes|public)/.*\.[cm]?js$)'` as 11-05. Reproduce 11-05's W reading (`2eb73ae0` vs `d7ceb373`) first to prove the instrument unchanged, then run `2eb73ae0` vs `af55cb73`. Run against checked-out/worktree copies of those commits, not the working tree.
* **Reuse 11-05's evidence tooling** (`import-walker.mjs`, `rulings-carry.py`, `build-report-tables.py`, `census-compare.py`, `ledger-11-05.tsv`, `rulings-11-05.tsv` in `_evidence-2026-11-05-drift/`): copy and re-point SHAs; no new tooling. If one cannot run, say so in the report and carry on as 11-05 did.
* **Ledger deltas are generated, not remembered.** Build the touch map the way `ledger-touch-map.txt` did: for every ledger row, its cited files × `git diff --numstat 2eb73ae0 af55cb73`. A row with a 0-line diff on every cited file is "unchanged (0-line diff)"; a touched file gets a hunk-level delta ("touched, not consolidated" is sharper than "unchanged"). Research expects 18 touched rows (12, 20, 24, 36, 37, 55, 63, 64, 81, 109, 111, 117, 119, 122, 123, 126, 129, 130; note 109 appears in that list but research also calls it a 0-line diff: **the script settles which**). If the script's list differs from research's, the script wins and the report says so.
* **Read all ten production commits' hunks (+717/−178).** This is the one thing that closes the census's blind spot (a decision moved inside a file whose census group kept its members). It is small enough to do fully; do not sample.
* **Cross-repo rows are unchanged by construction** (SD 0 commits; kit and `docs/runner-prompt.md` 0-line diff, verify with `git diff --stat`). Carry them as such; do not re-read SD as if it moved; do not rule on John's questions (e.g. halt cold-cache, LIN-4210/LIN-3024).
* **Say how big the window was and what it did to confidence** (10 production commits: "unchanged" is high-confidence for untouched files, lower for rows citing touched files).

### Where the decisions live: what to verify, per "one X" claim, and the repeatable search

Each is a claim to confirm or break at HEAD; report the search so a reader can rerun it.

| Claim | Verify by | Research's reading (to be checked, not copied) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| LIN-4253/4251/4277: a stage's route/writes/hint ladder held once | read `lib/stage-writes.js`, `prompt-template-defs.js`, `prompt-templates.js` (`stageWrites`), `proxy-preamble.js`, `dispatch-entrance.js`, `action-kind.js`, `prompts/stage-intent.js`; grep `endpointHintParts`, `SURVEY_KINDS`, `route === null`; check `public/llms.txt` and `lib/proxy-instructions.js` against the preamble ladder (two texts telling an agent the same thing); check `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` / `source-map.md` against code | holds; 9 per-kind tables still cost an edit, most are test-guarded lockstep (held); READING-vs-`writes` is two representations held equal by `lin-4253-stage-traits.test.js` (borderline, deliberate); `lib/stage-writes.js` sits in the guide's catch-all (Seams' gap: record, do not re-flag) |
| LIN-4263/4276: one posting-key list, one dispatch order | `postingKeysOf` in `lib/cost-read.js`, `byDispatchOrder` in `lib/lineage-membership.js`; grep other `dispatchedAt` sorts (`ci-wake-sweep.js`, `pipeline-loops.js`, `pipeline-churn.js`) and loader checks; rows 119, 122, 123, 129 | holds inside `/cost`; the "none re-writes it" comment overreaches; row 129 touched not consolidated (`cost-read.js:160`), 123 unchanged (`:212`), 122 improved by one site, 7+ sites unread |
| LIN-4247/4246/4293: one Go-state constructor, one "in progress", one focus rule | `goState`, `InProgress`, `focusInCard`; grep `go = {`, `activeElement` in `public/`; rows 103, 109, 128; `READY_TASK_STATE` | holds on Go; Home/task page files untouched; Observation twin is LIN-4238 (Backlog) |
| LIN-4252/4265/…/4255: fake-DOM consolidation holds the line | read `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js` (exact list, AST match, 25 files, 9 "stop"), `client-world.js`, `live-console-world.js`; count vm-over-`public/` suites without `loadWorld` | ratchet is real; `live-console-world.js` builds on `loadWorld` (not a second world); `loadWorld` half of the `CLAUDE.md` rule is unguarded |

**How I know I've found every place:** (a) the census (105 mustRule groups, identical membership expected), (b) the mechanical touch map for the ledger, (c) full read of all ten production diffs, (d) the repeatable greps above. **What this will not catch:** a decision duplicated in code not yet written, and changes inside guarded lockstep tables whose tests do not notice; the report states both. Research did not check at depth, and the builder must close or bound: the remaining cited sites of row 122, whether `docs/proxy-integration.md` restates the `/cost` `dispatches` contract, and the 22 mustRule groups whose sites shifted (run `rulings-carry.py`: a shift with unchanged members is not a consolidation).

### Decisions on the open questions (so the builder does not re-decide)

1. `override-kind-list-stale` **(low) — report as a finding, and mint one ticket.** It is the only candidate that is unticketed, cheap, has a concrete cost (an agent-facing text contract that omits `bug`, `plan-review`, `close-out`, `retrospective-audit`, which the route accepts), is mechanically testable (assert the catalog lists every key `hasPrompt` accepts, or interpolate from `PROMPT_TEMPLATES`, under "Unvalidated idea"), and is re-touched by every new stage kind (LIN-4248 edited it without deriving it). The 11-05 Backlog is stalled (`coherence-loop-stalled` unchanged: no Drift-family ticket moved), which argues for fewer tickets, not zero: this one is small enough to actually get worked. Before minting, rerun the Linear searches (`VERB OVERRIDE`, `kind list`, `override`, `accepts 19`) and the `docs/reviews` grep (`grep -rl "VERB OVERRIDE" docs/reviews` was 0). Parent under LIN-3449, `kind:follow-up`, default state, per earlier editions. If a ticket naming it turns up, note it instead.
2. **Lineage dispatch-order claim: a sub-item of row 79** `lineage-row-read-copies`**, not a new row or ticket.** The copies predate the window; what is new is one wrong comment. Delta: "worsened by a contradicting comment, copies unchanged". Not minted (the fix is a comment edit plus the row-79 consolidation, already tracked there).
3. **Fake-DOM** `loadWorld` **half: one new low row,** `world-helper-convention-half-guarded`**, report-only.** Bound it rather than leave "64 unclassified": a quick grep of the 64 suites for `document`/`window`/`dispatchEvent` use splits DOM-using from DOM-free; report both counts and the method. The per-suite quality is Code Quality's and coverage is Test Coverage's: cross-link, do not rule. Also search Linear for an existing ticket adding the three missing fake APIs (`getBoundingClientRect`, select value read/setter, bubbling `dispatchEvent`) that the nine "stop" entries wait on; if none, note it as the cause the ratchet's stops hang on, not a new ticket (the ratchet itself tracks them). Row 121 `unit-census-convention-split`: decide 5th allowlist shape vs one of the four in `drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04.md:102`; likely +1.
4. **Test tree scope: include the fake-DOM ratchet only** (a convention move, in remit). Do not run the census over `tests/` (excluded by the scope pattern, noisy, and owned by Code Quality/Test Coverage); say that in the report's scope audit.
5. **Survey place ledger: read last, read-only.** `git show origin/claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j:docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` (and notes/log); never check out or edit that branch. Record agree/disagree per ticket in one line; disagreement is a valid result. Do not shape findings to it.
6. **Preliminary verdict to test, not adopt:** stage templates/preamble better; cost read better (small); Go better, Home neutral; client test tree better with one gap; overall better, no mustRule movement, no new cycle. The report may overturn any of these if the hunks say so.

### Likeliest ways this breaks (and the witness for each)

1. **A row is called "unchanged" while a cited file was touched.** Witness: the generated touch map; every "unchanged" row's cited files show `0` in the numstat output committed in the evidence folder.
2. **The instrument is not the one 11-05 used, so deltas are noise.** Witness: the W-repro equals 11-05's readings on every key except the guide path (566 / 105 / 309 / 1; import graph 499/2,051 at the old commit); both full commit SHAs and the guide sha256 recorded in the report.
3. **The gate rejects Done or the PR is orphaned.** Witness: the single comment body contains a `github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/…` URL for the merged report plus `Adversarial second-read verdict:`, `Differed from top finding:`, `Disposition:` lines; the PR shows merged; the report's `## Adversarial Second-Read` section carries the same three fields, the tier, the question and the answer in full.
4. **The report touches more than the report.** Witness: `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` on the PR lists only `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-05-run4.md` and files under `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-05-drift-run4/`; the earlier edition files are byte-identical.
5. **Survey ledger contaminates the verdict.** Witness: the "Better or worse" section is committed in a working draft (or notes file in the evidence folder) before the ledger is first read; the report records the order.

This plan loosens no validation, contract or guard.

### Order of landing

1. Branch from `origin/main`; re-verify HEADs (`git rev-parse origin/main` both repos; if main moved, say so and do not widen the window: window bounds stay `2eb73ae0..af55cb73`).
2. Evidence: copy tools, W-repro, census at both ends, import graph, `res.status(` count (expect 275), touch map, `rulings-carry.py`. Write notes into the evidence folder as you go (the 11-05 edition needed four beats of notes; do the same so nothing is lost mid-session).
3. Read the ten production diffs; verify the four "one X" rows; scope-audit items (llms.txt, `proxy-instructions.js`, delivery scripts, place-change, docs); ticket re-check via `GET $HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE/api/proxy/issues/<id>` for the 23 carried tickets (LIN-4210, 4214, 4156, 4157, 4158, 3822, 3823, 3835, 3836, 3843, 3624, 3636, 3649, 3736, 3979, 1496, 3449, 2258, 4235, 4244, 4245, 4238, 2739).
4. Draft "Better or worse by area"; then read the place ledger; record agreement.
5. Write the report (headline, method, better/worse, findings severity-ranked and trend-framed, cross-repo verdicts, sibling hand-offs, classes and bounds, follow-ups incl. "considered and not minted", for John, ticket trend, census ruling table (105) and table groups (309), compact trend ledger of 130 + new rows). Keep it as long as the findings need; do not pad to match 11-05.
6. Mint follow-up (expected 1) after the duplicate search.
7. Second-read (Tier 2: a fresh-context sub-agent, no memory of this turn): give it only the window range, the repo and the one question ("what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"), and get its answer *before* showing it the report; then show the report for its verdict. Record `Differed from top finding` by comparing its own answer to the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict. A DISAGREE concludes the task normally; fix in place if cheap, else `escalated`.
8. Commit `LIN-4299: Drift & Coherence run 4 report (#PR)` (end the commit message with the attribution line from the session), open the PR (end the description with its attribution line), wait for `ci-success`, merge; post the one comment with the URL and the three fields plus the severity-ranked summary and one-line verdict; move LIN-4299 to Done.

### Session fit and review

**fits one session.** Research has done the discovery and the mechanical steps are scripted from 11-05's tooling; the judgment work (ten diffs, four verifications, a handful of rulings) is bounded.

## Research notes: LIN-4299 (Drift & Coherence run 4), research stage

**What this stage did.** This stage re-grounded the ticket, reproduced the instrument, took the HEAD readings, and read every production hunk in the window against the 11-05 ledger. It wrote no report, opened no PR, minted nothing and did not touch the Survey branch. Those are the review stage's deliverables. Everything below is evidence that stage can build on. Re-run the commands to regenerate the JSON: it lived in a session scratchpad and is not committed.

### 0. Re-grounding (staleness check)
- **HEADs did not move after the mint.** LinearViewer `origin/main` = `af55cb737ec4e63919bac65558b35498ede3d290`. SD `origin/main` = `07c88f7a338b3e19a01070775e1f4d4cfc91f040`. `git log --since=2026-11-05T19:31:52Z` is empty on both.
- **The window has 29 commits, not 28.** `git log --oneline 2eb73ae0..origin/main | wc -l` = 29. The ticket's own list includes `40557e9f` (the 11-05 report), so 29 is the right number.
- **Production:** 10 commits and 24 files, +717 / −178 (`git diff --shortstat 2eb73ae0 origin/main -- lib routes public server.js`). This matches the ticket.
- **Unchanged in the window (0-line diff):** `scripts/code-shape/`, `lib/runner-kit/`, `docs/runner-prompt.md`. The guide at HEAD has the same sha256 as at `2eb73ae0`: `e3194f52a76ed595a93ce3aa11b259dfce84114230f99596784243a7d994159f`. Using one guide for both runs is trivially the same file.
- **SD:** `07c88f7a..origin/main` = 0 commits. The cross-repo rows can only move on the Harbour side.
- **LIN-4269's 6 lines in `public/`** are `public/style.css:1793-1797`, a new `.opened-task-copy.copied` rule. The move onto the shared fake showed that the shared copy handler adds `copied` on the task surface too. This is a real (cosmetic) production change, not a test artefact.

### 1. Instrument and readings
| reading | 11-05 (`2eb73ae0`) | HEAD (`af55cb73`) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| census W-repro (`2eb73ae0` vs `d7ceb373`, guide `e3194f52…`) | 566 / 105 / 309 / 1 | the same; every JSON key equal except `areaGuide` (path) | the instrument is unchanged |
| census at HEAD vs `2eb73ae0` (the same guide, the same `--include '^(server\.js$\|(lib\|routes\|public)/.*\.[cm]?js$)'`) | — | 566 groups / **105 mustRule** / 309 table / 1 gone / 0 unranked | 562 unchanged, 2 grown, 1 shrunk, 1 new, 1 gone |
| import graph (11-05's `import-walker.mjs`) | 499 nodes / 2,051 static / 2 dynamic; SCCs 6+6; upward 0/0; route→route 53 | **500 / 2,053** / 2; SCCs 6+6, same members; 0/0; 53 | +`lib/stage-writes.js`; +2 edges, both into it (`prompt-template-defs.js`, `proxy-preamble.js`); 0 removed |
| `res.status(` in routes + server.js | 275 | 275 | 0 |

**Census movement, attributed to commits:**
- **No `mustRule` group left, shrank, grew or joined.** The 105 rulings carry over as-is. 22 of them only had their site lines shift; their members are unchanged.
- **Gone G0119 → new G0113** (table group). This is the stage-kind string set keyed in `STAGE_LEADS` / `STAGE_LABELS` / `BUCKET_OF_KIND`, now "+17" (was "+15"). LIN-4248 added both Survey kinds to all three tables in lockstep. That is a re-key, not a resolution (cf. ledger row 77 `census-gone-overstates-resolution`).
- **G0178 → G0173 grew** (table): `status == 'running'` went from 2 to 3 sites in `public/prompt-section.js` / `public/task-page.js`. The added site is the LIN-4247/4293 `endRun` / runPoll guard (`prompt-section.js:2407`).
- **G0171 → G0164 shrunk** and **G0164 → G0166 grew**. Both are anonymous tiny-helper groups. The first touches `public/question-cards.js` (the LIN-4293 `focusInCard` extraction). Noise.

### 2. Per-layer audit (claims verified against code at HEAD)

**L1. The stage templates and the preamble (LIN-4248, 4253, 4251, 4277).**
- **`route` and `writes` are now held once, on the template. The claim holds.** `EXCLUDED_FROM_AI_RECOMMENDATION` is derived from `route === null` (`lib/prompt-templates.js:425-427`). `rejectExcludedKind` reads `PROMPT_TEMPLATES[kind]?.route === null` (`lib/action-kind.js:19`). `SURVEY_KINDS` is gone. `writes` is declared on all 19 templates (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`: look-into `none` :282, triage `ticket-fields` :319, context `one-comment` :689, retro `none` :1135, the Surveys `one-comment` :1200/:1227, everything else `work`).
- **Both entrances resolve `writes` through one function.** That is `stageWrites` (`lib/prompt-templates.js:201-203`): `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1059,1085` and `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js:270,334`. The preamble validates the value (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:235-239`) and never imports the registry.
- **"One endpoint-hint ladder" (LIN-4277) holds within the file.** It is `endpointHintParts` / `renderEndpointHints` (`proxy-preamble.js:255-296`) plus one `CLOSING_LEAD_IN` (:197). No second ladder survives in `proxy-preamble.js`. Net −36 lines.
- **`lib/stage-writes.js` has no home in the area guide.** It matches only the catch-all "Other features" (`scripts/code-shape/areas.json`, regex check). The guide gap belongs to Seams. This review records it only.
- **Docs match the code.** `docs/architecture/source-map.md` and `prompt-system.md` agree with the writes value of each stage above, and with "19 templates".
- **Not consolidated: other per-kind traits still cost one edit per table.** LIN-4248 had to add the Survey kinds to 9 places: `PROMPT_TEMPLATES`, `COMPLETION_SIGNALS` (`lib/completion-signals.js:221-245`), `STAGE_INTENT` (`lib/prompts/stage-intent.js:32-33`), `GROUNDING_BY_KIND` (`lib/prompt-formatters.js:616`), `STAGE_LABELS` (`lib/run-view.js:73-74`), `BUCKET_OF_KIND` (`lib/wall-clock-summary.js:45`), `JOBS` (`lib/llm-jobs.js:54-55`), the agent catalog's VERB OVERRIDE list (`lib/proxy-instructions.js:860`), and `public/llms.txt` (list and the count "19"). Most of these are test-guarded completeness tables:
  - `run-view-stages.test.js:24` (every DISPATCH_KIND has a label);
  - `wall-clock-summary.test.js:191,196`;
  - `completion-signals.test.js:334`;
  - `llm-jobs-census.test.js`;
  - `prompt-templates.test.js:116` (exactly 19).
  That is the repo's accepted "guarded lockstep" convention, not drift. Ruling: borderline / held.
- **READING vs `writes`: two representations, held equal by a test.** A stage is READING in `STAGE_INTENT` exactly when its `writes` is `none`/`one-comment`. `tests/unit/lin-4253-stage-traits.test.js:113-125` enforces that ("related, not folded", a deliberate LIN-4251 decision). Ruling: borderline, guarded. Not a new row.
- **NEW candidate: `override-kind-list-stale` (low).** The agent-facing catalog `lib/proxy-instructions.js:860` lists 15 template keys for the VERB OVERRIDE. The route accepts all 19 (`hasPrompt`, `routes/proxy-compute.js:406`). Missing: `bug`, `plan-review`, `close-out`, `retrospective-audit`. The gap predates the window (since the LIN-2245 extraction, `937555cd`). LIN-4248 edited this same sentence (+2 Survey keys) without deriving it, so this is "touched, not consolidated". It is a text contract an agent acts on. The file is a template literal that could interpolate `Object.keys(PROMPT_TEMPLATES)` (an unvalidated idea). Searches: no prior review names it (`grep -rl "VERB OVERRIDE" docs/reviews` → 0), and Linear search "VERB OVERRIDE kind list" finds no open ticket.

**L2. The cost read (LIN-4263, 4276).**
- **"One posting-key list" holds in `/cost`.** It is `postingKeysOf` (`lib/cost-read.js:55-59`), used by `keyOf` (:62), `isPostingRow` (:195) and `dispatchesOf`. Outside `/cost`, row-key idioms (`row.id ?? row._id`: `dispatch-lineage-status.js:60`, `file-pointer.js:312`, `ci-wake-sweep.js:248`) predate the window. They are row keys, not posting keys. Not re-flagged.
- **"One dispatch order" is exported once** (`byDispatchOrder`, `lib/lineage-membership.js:60`) and reused by `dispatchesOf`.
- **NEW candidate, low/borderline: the claim overreaches.** The new comment at `lineage-membership.js:14-15` says readers that list dispatches "reuse it; none re-writes it". But `lib/ci-wake-sweep.js:253` sorts a lineage's rows (`rootItemId: lineageId`) by its own `toMs(a.dispatchedAt) - toMs(b.dispatchedAt)`, with a different no-time rule. `lib/pipeline-loops.js:84` (`?? 0`, no-time first) and `pipeline-churn.js:196` also have their own rule. These are pre-existing copies, plus a new comment that contradicts them. It sits closest to row 79 `lineage-row-read-copies`. Decide there: a sub-item or a new row.
- **Row 129 `request-source-guard-copies` is touched, not consolidated.** `cost-read.js` was edited (+139) and its inline loader check moved from :147 to **:160**, still inline. `run-view.js:391` and `kpi-stats.js:1067` are unchanged.
- **Row 123 `completeness-precedence-restated` is unchanged.** It moved from `cost-read.js:199` to **:212**. `row-usage.js:116` and `request-usage-fold.js:105` are unchanged.
- **Row 119 `cost-fold-partition-restated`: held resolved.** `countedRowsOf` is still the only partition.
- **Row 122 `usage-snapshot-prose-residue`: partly re-touched.** LIN-4263 rewrote `lib/proxy-instructions.js:384-386`, and the "cumulative worker usage snapshots" phrase is gone there (`grep -n -i snapshot lib/proxy-instructions.js` now hits only the new `dispatches` prose at :395). So 1 more of the 9 cited sites is fixed. The other 7 still need re-reading.
- **The per-dispatch split is opt-in (`perDispatch`) and only `/cost` passes it** (`routes/proxy-compute.js:743`). No bystander cost for the Models page, routing preview or effort readout.

**L3. Go, Home and task-page state (LIN-4247, 4246, 4293).**
- **"One Go-state constructor" holds.** `goState(status, fields)` (`public/prompt-section.js:262`) replaces every `state.go = {…}` literal. One read-side fallback survives: `state.go || { status: 'ready' }` (:291). Ruling: noise.

They read the server's facts (`lib/task-state.js:55-64` `sessionFactsOf`). `ended` is a new client rule (LIN-4247), but it composes server facts and adds no new literal. Census: `status == 'running'` gained 1 site (G0173).

The Observation twin `rulingRowHoldsInput` (`public/observation.js:2138-2145`, with a different focus rule: field tags only) is unchanged. It is tracked by **LIN-4238** (Backlog, 0 comments).
- **Rows 103 `home-next-answer-split`, 109 `task-page-state-outside-owner` and 128 `waiting-standing-comment-residue` are unchanged with high confidence.** `lib/render-task-page.js`, `public/task-page.js`, `public/app.js`, `lib/home-row-states.js`, `lib/waiting-section.js` and `lib/home-view.js` all have a 0-line diff. `READY_TASK_STATE` is still at `render-task-page.js:108`.

**L4. The client test tree (fake-DOM consolidation, LIN-4252/4265/4266–4285/4270/4272/4255).**
- **The ratchet is real.** `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js` uses an exact sorted file list, not a count (:22-26). It matches by AST shape, not by name. It scans `tests`, `scripts/eval` and `scripts/code-shape`. It lists **25 files, 9 of them annotated "stop"**. Each stop names the fake API that is missing: `getBoundingClientRect`, a select value read/setter, a bubbling `dispatchEvent`. So a stop is a gap in the shared fake, not a reasoned permanent exemption. No ticket was found that adds those three APIs; the review stage should search.
